newsitem.title: USA: General Mills nudges estimates down - analysts.
newsitem.headline: General Mills nudges estimates down - analysts.

text.p: General Mills Inc indicated in a conference call with analysts Wednesday that its earnings for fiscal 1997, ending in May, may be less than originally planned, analysts said.

"They said basically that the consensus of estimates has been about $3.10 (per share for fiscal 1997). They are more comfortable with $3.05, and even that is not entirely assured," said Schroder Wertheim managing director Robert Cummins.
Shares of General Mills were down 1-3/8 at 63-3/8 at midday.
General Mills officials were not available for comment.
The analysts said the company still expects fiscal 1997 earnings to be higher than the year-earlier $3.00 a share.
They said General Mills's current guidance for fiscal 1997 indicates the company could post lower earnings for the fourth quarter, compared with the $0.49 a share of a year earlier.
Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette analyst William Leach said the company's guidance indicated "a slight down fourth quarter."
Yesterday Leach upgraded General Mills to neutral from underperform based on its price and yield.
Earlier today General Mills, the second largest U.S. cereal maker, said it expected unit volume, which was down in the third quarter, to grow in the fourth quarter.
"The strength of that volume increase will be the key factor determining our annual earnings gain," Chairman Stephen Sanger said in a statement.
Shares of Kellogg Co, the top U.S. cereal company, were off one at 67-1/2 at midday. Analysts cited concern about the sluggish U.S. ready-to-eat cereal market.
General Mills said that for the first nine months of its fiscal year, domestic cereal volume was up one percent.
